title: Query-optimal quantum simulation of Lindblad evolution
abstract: For the problem of simulating Lindblad evolution for time $t$ to precision $ε$, Hamiltonian simulation provides an additive query lower bound, informally, $Ω(t + \mathrm{polylog}(1/ε))$. However, the best previously known algorithms for general Lindblad simulation achieve a multiplicative upper bound, informally, $\mathcal{O}(t\,\mathrm{polylog}(1/ε))$, in gate complexity. It has remained open whether this multiplicative dependence is necessary. In this paper, we close the gap in query complexity by giving an algorithm with optimal additive dependence on evolution time and precision in the block-encoding model. Our approach uses the transducer framework to reduce the query cost of composing first-order approximations to the evolution channel, together with linear combinations of reuse circuits of different lengths to suppress catalyst-removal error.   Although our additional gate complexity is higher than that of existing algorithms, our optimal query complexity resolves the question of how much oracle access is fundamentally necessary and identifies the remaining challenge to achieve the optimal gate complexity.
summary: This paper develops a quantum circuit algorithm to simulate Lindblad evolution, which models open quantum systems. By using a transducer framework, the authors achieve an optimal additive query complexity, resolving a long-standing question about the necessary scaling of resources. This result is significant for understanding the fundamental computational limits of simulating dissipative quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental query complexity required to simulate Lindblad evolution for open quantum systems over a given time $t$ to a precision $\epsilon$. It aims to close the gap between the known lower and upper bounds for this simulation.
main_result: The authors provide an algorithm achieving optimal additive query complexity, $O(	au + 	ext{polylog}(	au/\epsilon))$, for general Lindblad simulation in the block-encoding model. This proves that the multiplicative dependence on time previously suspected was not a fundamental necessity in this model.
method: The approach utilizes a transducer framework, combining local dissipative transducers with Hamiltonian transducers, and employs linear combinations of reuse circuits to manage error accumulation.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system whose dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation. The simulation is implemented using quantum circuits within the block-encoding model.
key_observables: The primary observable is the approximation of the quantum channel $e^{Lt}$ representing the evolution of the density matrix $ho$.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the evolution time $t$, the desired precision $\epsilon$, and the total evolution time $	au$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the block-encoding model, and the gate complexity of the resulting algorithm is noted to be higher than existing methods.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of Lindblad simulation, details the use of transducers for composition, addresses error control (including catalyst-removal error), and extends the method to time-dependent generators.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the resource scaling (query complexity) for simulating open quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum simulation algorithms in AMO physics and quantum optics.
